He sent Linghu Xingda to murder the emperor in the palace, seized dozens of courtiers who opposed him along with numerous imperial affines, and slaughtered them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Prince Xiao of Qin, whom he enthroned as puppet emperor.
秦孝王 is the princely title Prince Xiao of Qin, not an emperor named Xiaojing.

He sent Linghu Xingda to assassinate the emperor within the palace; he also seized several tens of court ministers who did not agree with him and various imperial affines, killing them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Emperor Xiaojing of Qin, whom he set up as emperor.

He sent Linghu Xingda to assassinate the emperor within the palace; he also seized several tens of court ministers who did not agree with him and various imperial affines, killing them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Prince Xiao of Qin, whom he set up as emperor.
The same 秦孝王 phrase is princely, so Emperor Xiaojing of Qin is a mistranslation in the literal line as well.
Yuwen Huaji—Yuwen Huaji was the son of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Yiwu Guard.
Yuwen Huaji was the son of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Yiwei Guard.
The Chinese names 宇文化及 once, and 左翊衞 is Yiwei, not Yiwu; the doubled lemma and guard name are both errors.
Li Mi sent Xu Jixing to hold the Liyang granary.
Li Mi sent Xu Ji to hold the Liyang granary.
徐勣 is Xu Ji; Jixing is not a reading of 勣.
Li Mi sent Xu Jixing to hold Liyang granary.
Li Mi sent Xu Ji to hold Liyang granary.
The literal line repeats the same false given name for 徐勣.
Huaji was carted to Hejian, charged repeatedly with regicide, and beheaded with his sons Chenggi and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to the Turkic Princess Yicheng and displayed on the frontier.
Huaji was carted to Hejian, charged repeatedly with regicide, and beheaded with his sons Chengji and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to the Turkic Princess Yicheng and displayed on the frontier.
承基 is Chengji; Chenggi invents a different spelling of the same characters.

Then they loaded Huaji on a caged cart to Hejian, repeatedly charged him with the crime of killing his sovereign, and beheaded him together with his two sons Chenggi and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to Princess Yicheng of the Turks and displayed in the barbarian court.

Then they loaded Huaji on a caged cart to Hejian, repeatedly charged him with the crime of killing his sovereign, and beheaded him together with his two sons Chengji and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to Princess Yicheng of the Turks and displayed in the barbarian court.
The literal line has the same Chenggi error for 承基.
In Daye year three he became hawk-raising gentleman.
In Daye year three he became Eagle-soaring Gentleman.
鷹揚郎將 is the Sui Yingyang command, an eagle-soaring military office, not a hawk-raising post.
In the third year of Daye he became Hawk-raising Gentleman.
In the third year of Daye he became Eagle-soaring Gentleman.
The literal Hawk-raising Gentleman repeats the same mistranslation of 鷹揚.
Sima Dekan—Sima Dekan was a man of Yong in Fufeng.
Sima Dekan was a man of Yong in Fufeng.
司馬德戡 appears once before 扶風雍人也; the em-dash name doubling is not in the Chinese.
At Jiangdu he commanded ten thousand elite personal guards within the city.
Following the emperor to Jiangdu, he commanded ten thousand elite personal guards encamped within the city.
從至江都 records that he followed to Jiangdu, and 營於城內 that the ten thousand guards were encamped inside the city; both are missing from the original idiomatic line.

At Xuzhou they disembarked; Huaji put Dekan in the rear guard while he plotted with Zhao Xingshu, Li Ben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others to strike Huaji and sent envoys to Meng Haigong for aid.

At Xuzhou they disembarked; Huaji ordered Dekan to command the rear guard, and Dekan with Zhao Xingshu, Li Ben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others plotted to surprise Huaji, sending men to Meng Haigong to ally as external aid.
After 令德戡將後軍, the silent subject of 乃與…謀襲化及 is Dekan; the original he after Huaji makes Huaji plot against himself.
On accession he promoted old intimates, making Qiantong Xuanhui captain then direct gate attendant.
On accession he promoted old intimates, appointing Qiantong as Xuanhui captain then transferring him to direct gate attendant.
授宣惠尉 names the office Xuanhui captain; Qiantong Xuanhui wrongly fuses the person with the title.
Shichong's father was raised by Can after the remarriage; Shichong took the Wang surname and his father became prefect of Huai and Bian.
His father, a young orphan, followed his mother when she married Can; Can loved and raised him, so he took the Wang surname and rose to chief administrator of Huai and Bian.
因姓王氏 and 官至懷、汴二州長史 continue the career of 其父, the orphan raised by Can, not Shichong; 長史 is chief administrator, not prefect.
Shichong's father took in the young orphan; following his mother's remarriage to Can, Can loved and raised him, and therefore he took the surname Wang, rising to prefect of Huai and Bian prefectures.
His father, orphaned young, followed his mother when she married Can; Can loved and raised him, and therefore he took the surname Wang, rising to chief administrator of Huai and Bian prefectures.
其父 is himself the young orphan raised by Can, not an adopter of a third child, and 長史 is chief administrator; “received as a young orphan” is an awkward rendering of 收幼孤.
When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Fen of Wu and Guan Chong of Jingling raised a hundred thousand in Jiangnan.
When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling raised troops in Jiangnan in response, styled themselves generals, and mustered more than a hundred thousand.
爕 is Xie, not Fen, but the proposed line still writes Jingling for 晉陵 and drops 起兵…以應之, 自稱將軍, and 十餘萬.
Following Wendu and Lu Chu's plan, Tong appointed Li Mi grand marshal; Mi submitted, fought Huaji at Liyang, and reported victory.
Following Wendu and Lu Chu's plan, Tong appointed Li Mi grand marshal and secretariat director; Mi submitted, fought Huaji at Liyang, and reported victory.
拜李密為太尉、尚書令 confers both Grand Marshal and Secretariat Director; the original idiomatic line omits 尚書令.
The day was set until Duan Da's son-in-law Zhang Zhi exposed Chu's plot.
The day had already been set when General Duan Da sent his son-in-law Zhang Zhi to report Chu's plot.
期有日矣 means a date was already fixed, not that action waited until Zhang Zhi spoke; the proposal’s “had arrived” overreads 有日矣 and still drops 將軍段達遣.
Soon Shichong had Wei Jie urge Tong to name him left vice minister and supreme commander.
Soon Shichong had Wei Jie urge Tong to name him left vice director of the department of state affairs and commander of all internal and external military affairs.
尚書左僕射 is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and 總督內外諸軍事 is command of inner and outer armies, not a vague supreme commander.
Brother Wei and son Xuanying, prisoners of Mi since following Huaji, were recovered.
Shichong's elder brother Wei and his son Xuanying, who had followed Huaji to Dong commandery and been imprisoned by Mi, were all recovered.
充兄偉及子玄應隨化及至東郡 identifies Shichong’s elder brother and son and the Dong commandery captivity omitted in the original.
He seized kin of Mi's officers, comforted them, and had them summon their men.

He also seized the wives and children of Mi's chief clerk Bing Yuanzhen, the mother of aide-de-camp Zheng Qianxiang, and the sons and younger brothers of various generals, comforted them, and had each secretly call their fathers and elder brothers.
邴元真 is Bing Yuanzhen, not Xing, and the line names his wives and children, Zheng Qianxiang’s mother, and the generals’ sons and younger brothers.
Duan Da—Duan Da was a man of Guzang in Wuwei.
Duan Da was a man of Guzang in Wuwei.
段達 appears once in 段達，武威姑臧人也; the doubled lemma is not in the Chinese.
He pacified Fang and Chu in Gao Zhihui's rebellion, received a thousand bolts of silk, and rose to honored companion.
When Gao Zhihui, Li Ji, and others rebelled, Da led ten thousand men, pacified Dingfang and Chu prefectures, received a thousand bolts of silk, and was promoted to honored companion.
The rebels are 高智惠、李積等, Da led 眾一萬, and the prefectures are 定方、滁, not Fang and Chu alone.
He was soon restored as general of the Left Yiwu Guard.
He was soon restored as general of the Left Yiwei Guard.
左翊衞將軍 is General of the Left Yiwei Guard; Yiwu mistranscribes 翊衞.
Before long he was again appointed General of the Left Yiwu Guard.
Before long he was again appointed General of the Left Yiwei Guard.
The literal line has the same Yiwu error for 左翊衞將軍.
When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Wendu enthroned Prince Yue Tong, made him opening-the-government honored companion, chief speaker, and Duke of Chen.

When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Wendu and others installed Prince Yue Tong as ruler; Da was appointed opening-the-government honored companion, concurrently chief speaker, and enfeoffed Duke of Chen.
After 推越王侗為主, 署開府儀同三司，兼納言，封陳國公 are Da’s offices and enfeoffment, not titles given to Tong.

When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Yuan Wendu and others installed Prince Yue Tong as ruler, appointed him Opening the Government with Honored Companion of the Third Rank, concurrently Chief Speaker, and enfeoffed him Duke of Chen.

When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Yuan Wendu and others installed Prince Yue Tong as ruler; Da was appointed Opening the Government with Honored Companion of the Third Rank, concurrently Chief Speaker, and enfeoffed Duke of Chen.
The silent subject of 署 and 封 is Da, the biography subject, not Prince Yue Tong.
